title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons, and say what is about to happen ('it's going to rain').
intro: Gujarat has three main seasons: a long hot **ઉનાળો** (summer), the **ચોમાસું** (monsoon) from June to September, and a pleasant **શિયાળો** (winter). Weather talk in Gujarati is mostly impersonal: 'heat is' (**ગરમી છે**), 'rain falls' (**વરસાદ પડે છે**). You'll also learn the handy **-વાનું છે** construction for 'is going to / is about to'.

vocab.note: f · ઠંડી is unpleasant cold, ઠંડક welcome cool

phrases.en: It's cold outside — wear a sweater.
There are clouds in the sky.
It's very sunny — let's sit in the shade.

phrases.native: મને શિયાળો સૌથી વધારે ગમે છે.
phrases.roman: mane shiyāḷo sauthī vadhāre game chhe.

phrases.native: લાગે છે કે આજે વરસાદ આવશે.
phrases.roman: lāge chhe ke āje varsād āvshe.
phrases.en: It looks like it'll rain today.

grammar.title: Weather expressions are impersonal
grammar.body:
Gujarati weather sentences have no 'it'. The weather itself is the subject:

**ગરમી છે** 'it's hot' (lit. 'heat is'), **ઠંડી છે** 'it's cold', **તડકો છે** 'it's sunny', **ભેજ છે** 'it's humid'.
**વરસાદ પડે છે / આવે છે** 'it's raining' (lit. 'rain falls / comes').
**પવન ફૂંકાય છે** 'the wind is blowing'.

How you **feel** the weather uses the dative + **લાગવું** (Unit 9): **મને ગરમી લાગે છે** 'I feel hot'. Note the difference: **ગરમી છે** describes the day; **મને ગરમી લાગે છે** describes you.

With **થવું** 'to become', you describe a change: **ઠંડી થઈ ગઈ** 'it's turned cold'.

examples.native: અમદાવાદમાં મે મહિનામાં બહુ ગરમી હોય છે.
examples.roman: Amdāvādmāṃ me mahināmāṃ bahu garmī hoy chhe.
examples.en: In Ahmedabad it's very hot in May.
It gets cool in the evening.

grammar.title: 'Going to / about to': -વાનું છે
grammar.body:
To say something **is going to happen** or **is about to happen**, take the infinitive, change **-વું** to **-વાનો / -વાની / -વાનું** (agreeing with the subject), and add **છે**:

**વરસાદ પડવાનો છે** 'it's going to rain' (વરસાદ is masculine)
**ટ્રેન આવવાની છે** 'the train is about to arrive' (ટ્રેન is feminine)
**હું જવાનો છું / જવાની છું** 'I'm going to go' (man / woman)

It expresses a plan or an expectation, like English 'going to'. You'll see it again for future plans in Unit 17.

examples.en: I'm going to go to the beach. (woman)

dialogue.title: Monsoon plans
dialogue.setting: Two friends, Parth and Sneha, look out of the window on a cloudy July morning.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.en: Look how many clouds there are in the sky!

lines.speaker: Parth
lines.native: હા, લાગે છે કે ધોધમાર વરસાદ પડવાનો છે.
lines.roman: hā, lāge chhe ke dhodhmār varsād paḍvāno chhe.
lines.en: Yes, it looks like it's going to pour.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: આપણે આજે ડુંગર પર જવાનાં હતાં ને?
lines.roman: āpaṇe āje ḍuṅgar par javānāṃ hatāṃ ne?
lines.en: Weren't we going to go up the hill today?

lines.speaker: Parth
lines.native: હા, પણ વરસાદમાં રસ્તો બહુ ભીનો હશે.
lines.roman: hā, paṇ varsādmāṃ rasto bahu bhīno hashe.
lines.en: Yes, but in the rain the path will be very wet.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: મને તો ચોમાસું બહુ ગમે છે. બધું લીલું થઈ જાય છે.
lines.roman: mane to chomāsuṃ bahu game chhe. badhuṃ līluṃ thaī jāy chhe.
lines.en: I really love the monsoon. Everything turns green.

lines.speaker: Parth
lines.native: સાચી વાત. અને ગરમી પણ ઓછી થાય છે.
lines.roman: sāchī vāt. ane garmī paṇ ochhī thāy chhe.
lines.en: True. And the heat goes down too.

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: તો ચાલ, ઘરે ભજિયાં અને ચા બનાવીએ!
lines.roman: to chāl, ghare bhajiyāṃ ane chā banāvīe!
lines.en: So come on, let's make bhajiyas and tea at home!

culture: The first monsoon rain is a celebration in Gujarat: people head out to eat hot **ભજિયાં** (pakoras) and **મકાઈ** (roasted corn) in the rain. Summer temperatures in Ahmedabad regularly reach 45°C, so afternoon life slows down. Winter brings **ઉત્તરાયણ** (14 January), when the whole state flies kites from the rooftops.

lessons.title: Saying if it's hot or cold

tip.title: Weather has no 'it'
tip.body:
- The weather itself is the subject: **ગરમી છે** 'it's hot' (lit. 'heat is'), **ઠંડી છે** 'it's cold', **તડકો છે** 'it's sunny', **ભેજ છે** 'it's humid'.
- How *you* feel it: **મને** ગરમી **લાગે છે** 'I feel hot'.
- ગરમી and ઠંડી are feminine: ગરમી **હતી**, ઠંડી **નથી લાગતી**.
tip.pattern: આજે + ગરમી / ઠંડી + છે · મને ગરમી લાગે છે

sentences.en: It's very cold today.
I feel really hot.
Are you cold?
I don't feel cold.
It was very hot yesterday.

sentences.native: આજે ગરમી ઓછી છે, પણ ભેજ બહુ છે.
sentences.roman: āje garmī ochhī chhe, paṇ bhej bahu chhe.
sentences.en: It's not so hot today, but it's very humid.
The weather is really nice today.
It's very sunny today.
It's nice and cool outside.

tip.title: Rain "falls"
tip.body:
- In Gujarati rain **falls**: **વરસાદ પડે છે** 'it's raining'. You'll also hear વરસાદ **આવે** છે.
- વરસાદ is masculine, so the verb is masculine: વરસાદ **પડ્યો** 'it rained', વરસાદ **નથી પડતો** 'it isn't raining'.
- વાદળ 'cloud' is neuter; 'clouds' is **વાદળાં**.

sentences.en: Is it raining outside?
It's raining gently.
It rained a lot last night.
It rained a lot this month.
It isn't raining today.
There isn't a single cloud in the sky.
There's lightning in the sky.

sentences.native: આજે વાદળાં છે, પણ વરસાદ નથી.
sentences.roman: āje vādaḷāṃ chhe, paṇ varsād nathī.
sentences.en: It's cloudy today, but there's no rain.
It's very windy outside.

sentences.native: વીજળી ગઈ છે, પંખો નથી ચાલતો.
sentences.roman: vījaḷī gaī chhe, paṅkho nathī chālto.
sentences.en: The power's gone, the fan isn't working.

lessons.title: It's going to rain

tip.title: Going to: -વાનો છે
tip.body:
- Change **-વું** to **-વાનો / -વાની / -વાનું** (agreeing with the subject) and add **છે**: વરસાદ **પડવાનો** છે 'it's going to rain'.
- વરસાદ (m) → પડવાનો; ગરમી (f) → **વધવાની**; વાવાઝોડું (n) → **આવવાનું**.
- For people: હું **જવાનો** છું (man), હું **જવાની** છું (woman).

new: લાગે છે કે આજે વરસાદ આવશે.

sentences.en: It's going to rain this afternoon.
A storm is coming tonight.
It's going to get hotter this week.
The monsoon is coming soon.
The bus is about to come, hurry up!
I'm going to go out. (man)
Everything got wet in the rain.
My clothes are wet.
Are the clothes dry?
It rains a lot in the monsoon.

lessons.title: Talking about the seasons

tip.title: Seasons and 'in'
tip.body:
- Add **-માં** for 'in', changing a final -ઓ or -ઉં to -આ first: ઉનાળો → **ઉનાળામાં**, શિયાળો → **શિયાળામાં**, ચોમાસું → **ચોમાસામાં**.
- 'I like …' is **મને … ગમે છે**: મને શિયાળો ગમે છે.
- For what's usually true, use **હોય છે**: ઉનાળામાં ગરમી **હોય છે**.

new: મને શિયાળો સૌથી વધારે ગમે છે.

sentences.en: It's very hot in summer.
In winter it's cold in the mornings.
The sunshine feels nice in winter.
Do you like summer?

sentences.native: મને આ ઋતુ બહુ ગમે છે.
sentences.roman: mane ā rutu bahu game chhe.
sentences.en: I really like this season.
How many seasons are there in your country?

sentences.native: ભારતમાં ત્રણ ઋતુઓ છે: ઉનાળો, ચોમાસું અને શિયાળો.
sentences.roman: Bhāratmāṃ traṇ rutuo chhe: unāḷo, chomāsuṃ ane shiyāḷo.
sentences.en: India has three seasons: summer, monsoon and winter.

sentences.native: આજે રાત્રે આકાશમાં બહુ તારા છે.
sentences.roman: āje rātre ākāshmāṃ bahu tārā chhe.
sentences.en: There are lots of stars in the sky tonight.
Look, how beautiful the moon is!
Don't look at the sun.
This tree is very tall.
Come on, let's sit under the tree.

sentences.native: આ લાલ ફૂલ બહુ સુંદર છે.
sentences.roman: ā lāl fūl bahu sundar chhe.
sentences.en: This red flower is very beautiful.
I love the sea.
Shall we go to the beach on Sunday?
It's pleasantly cool up in the hills.
There are lots of animals in the forest.
There are two birds in the tree.
Which animal do you like?

sentences.native: મારા ગામમાં ઘણાં ઝાડ અને ફૂલો છે.
sentences.roman: mārā gāmmāṃ ghaṇāṃ jhāḍ ane fūlo chhe.
sentences.en: There are lots of trees and flowers in my village.
